question: Where did Subhash Chandra Bose form the "Provisional Government of Free India"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Singapore**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose formed the **"Provisional Government of Free India"** in Singapore on October 21, 1943.
 
• The Provisional Government of Free India was also known as **Azad Hind Government**.
 
• This government was established during World War II and was supported by the Axis powers.
 
• The formation of this government was a part of Bose's efforts to secure Indian independence from British rule.
 
• Under Bose's leadership, the Indian National Army (INA) was also revived to fight against the British forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Subhash Chandra Bose was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement and is remembered for his radical approach towards achieving independence.
 
• Bose's famous slogan was **"Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!"**
 
• The INA, under Bose's command, fought alongside Japanese forces in the Burma Campaign against the British Indian Army.
 
• Despite initial successes, the INA faced setbacks and was eventually defeated, but Bose’s efforts left a lasting impact on India's struggle for independence.
 
• After the war, the trials of INA officers by the British ignited widespread nationalist sentiments in India.
